text: Re-scoped and MEASURED 2026-09-25: NOT a zoom-cull or camera/perf-mod bug. Root cause is vanilla body-hidden-when-swimming rendering: PawnRenderNodeWorker_Body.CanDrawNow() returns false when PawnRenderFlags.NoBody is set (set when Pawn.Swimming=CurJob.swimming); PawnRenderNodeWorker_Head never checks NoBody, so the head keeps drawing. Screenshot proof: Holmes (Human822690) at (112,12) renders as a floating head with no body above the beach line. get_cell_info confirms (112,12) terrain=RUT_ScaldMargin -- our own WaterShallowBase-derived custom terrain (TerminalBiomes/Defs/TerrainDefs/RUT_ScaldMargin.xml) -- so vanilla correctly reads him as standing in water and hides the body; this part is not a bug. Hicks vanishes on dry Sand nearby, consistent with a stale CurJob.swimming flag not clearing after leaving our water, combined with PawnRenderer's useCached path (Find.CameraDriver.ZoomRootSize>18f uses a cached humanlike atlas; <=18f always renders the live tree honoring whatever NoBody state is current) -- this explains the zoom-dependent flicker without any screen-rect culling bug. Ollopom/RM_Shulla vanishing but Dactillion/RM_Noohm not tracks the same mechanism via DrawNonHumanlikeSwimmingGraphic: only PawnKindDefs with swimmingGraphicData set get a swim sprite when Swimming; without one a submerged small animal falls into the same suppressed-body rendering. title: shared_sync.py silently drops a peer commit made during its run: reset --keep moves HEAD past work that was never in its todo set, and origin/main..HEAD then reads clean
spec: MEASURED 2026-09-26: a 16-file commit by the Grey Sea build agent vanished from HEAD during a peer's shared_sync.py run; git log origin/main..HEAD printed nothing, which reads as 'all pushed'. Recovered byte-exact from the dropped commit's blobs. MECHANISM, read off src/RimMandrake/Utils/shared_sync.py: todo is computed at ~line 78 (git rev-list --cherry-pick --right-only UP...HEAD), the replay+push publishes exactly that set, then ~line 123 runs git reset --keep UP. One tree, one HEAD, four agents => any commit that lands on HEAD between those two points is never in todo, is never pushed, and reset --keep moves HEAD past it. No warning; survives only in the reflog. FIX: re-read HEAD immediately before the reset and compare it to the HEAD todo was computed from; if it moved, abort (or loop) rather than reset. Until fixed, every caller must prove survival with git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main. Recorded in CLAUDE.md's Git section.

title: One gravship can only ever visit ONE sea floor: MapPortal caches its pocket map, so the hatch's per-tile biome resolution runs once and every later dive re-enters the first sea
spec: MEASURED 2026-09-26 from the decompiled engine (RimSage, RimWorld/MapPortal.cs lines 12-340) plus our own source. DEFECT: RM_SeaDiveHatch (src/RimMandrake/DivingInteraction/Source/RM_SeaDiveHatch.cs) overrides ONLY GeneratePocketMapInt(). In vanilla MapPortal, GetOtherMap() reads 'if (PocketMap == null) GeneratePocketMap();' and GeneratePocketMap() is the ONLY caller of GeneratePocketMapInt(). The field 'protected Map pocketMap' is Scribed (Scribe_References.Look(ref pocketMap, "pocketMap")) and is nulled only when map.Parent?.HasMap == false. => The pocket map is generated ONCE per hatch and reused forever. CONSEQUENCE: the hatch is a building on the gravship and travels with it. Dive at the Twilight Sea -> ResolveGeneratorForCurrentTile() picks RM_SeaDiveGenerator_TwilightSea, generates, caches. Fly to the Grey Sea and dive -> PocketMap is non-null, so GeneratePocketMapInt() is never called again and the party re-enters the TWILIGHT floor. Three of the four seas are unreachable to a given ship after its first dive. The per-tile resolution in ResolveGeneratorForCurrentTile() is careful and correct and is DEAD CODE after the first dive, which is why the class reads as right. Note the vanilla 'view pocket map' gizmo also hardcodes def.portal.pocketMapGenerator.label, so a Twilight hatch will mislabel too. FIX SHAPE (not ruled): either key a map per sea on the hatch (a Dictionary<string biomeDefName, Map>, all Scribed) and override GetOtherMap() to select by the parent map's current biome, or release/regenerate when the current tile's sea differs from the cached map's. Persistence-vs-regenerate is owner question 8 of design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_twilight_deep_bedazzle_2026-09-26.md - a persisted floor per sea is the richer answer and is what players will expect after building a base down there.
